INT-01.speaker: Mara
INT-01.caption: There you are. I'm Mara, Head of Engineering. Short version of my job: when two smart people disagree, I get the headache.

INT-02.speaker: Mara
INT-02.caption: I brought you in because I need someone who looks at the evidence, not at whoever is loudest in the room.

INT-03.speaker: Dev
INT-03.caption: I'm Dev, I lead robotics. My team builds the robot's movement and autonomy.

INT-04.speaker: Dev
INT-04.caption: We've got it sorting full trays without help. I want Northgate to see that progress, and I know the safety concerns need an answer.

INT-05.speaker: Ines
INT-05.caption: Ines. Software and Safety. I make sure the robot stops when it's supposed to stop.

INT-06.speaker: Ines
INT-06.caption: I want us to demonstrate the robot without putting anyone at risk. We need to know exactly how it stops.

INT-07.speaker: Dev
INT-07.caption: I hear you. I just don't want us to lose what makes the prototype useful.

INT-08.speaker: Ines
INT-08.caption: Then let's look at the tests together.

INT-09.speaker: Mara
INT-09.caption: That's where you come in. Help us turn that disagreement into a plan we can both stand behind.

BRF-01.speaker: Mara
BRF-01.caption: Here's the situation. We're Halyard Robotics, building a warehouse robot called TERN-1.

BRF-02.speaker: Mara
BRF-02.caption: Our customer, Northgate, watches a live demo in twelve weeks. They want two things that don't naturally get along: a robot that works on its own, and a paper trail proving a human can override it.

BRF-03.speaker: Mara
BRF-03.caption: Dev says speed and autonomy win the contract. Ines says safeguards win it. They're both partly right, and they've stopped listening to each other.

BRF-04.speaker: Mara
BRF-04.caption: Your job, in six moves: check the evidence, settle three arguments, show the team the data, choose the robot's settings, run the demo, then see what happened.

BRF-05.speaker: Mara
BRF-05.caption: Watch the gauges at the top. Resentment, runway, readiness, team alignment, and your credibility. Every choice moves them.

BRF-06.speaker: Mara
BRF-06.caption: You can't check everything. You get three investigations, five persuasion points, and three chances to step in during the demo. Spend them like they matter.

BRF-07.speaker: Mara
BRF-07.caption: Nobody is grading you on being right. They're watching what you do with the evidence. Ready?

GUIDE-FLOOR.speaker: Mara
GUIDE-FLOOR.caption: Five things in this room could change how we argue. You can look closely at three.

GUIDE-TABLE.speaker: Mara
GUIDE-TABLE.caption: Three arguments are on this table. For each one, drop a token on who you back.

GUIDE-CONSEQUENCE1.speaker: Ines
GUIDE-CONSEQUENCE1.caption: You've settled the three arguments. This next screen shows how Dev and Ines reacted to the choices you just made.

GUIDE-DATA.speaker: Dev
GUIDE-DATA.caption: We have four sets of test results. Choose which ones we show the team, and we'll work through what they mean.

GUIDE-FORGE.speaker: Mara
GUIDE-FORGE.caption: Now the real choices. Speed, recovery, learning. And remember, a question mark means nobody measured it.

GUIDE-RUN.speaker: Mara
GUIDE-RUN.caption: Five events. The action pauses before each choice, so no countdown panic.

GUIDE-ENDING.speaker: Mara
GUIDE-ENDING.caption: The demo is over. Now let us look at what your decisions made possible.

GUIDE-DEBRIEF.speaker: Mara
GUIDE-DEBRIEF.caption: You can rewind a decision without erasing the run you just made.

DISC-E1.speaker: Dev
DISC-E1.caption: The robot kept moving as someone crossed its path. We need to understand the stopping margin before we show this to Northgate.

DISC-E2.speaker: Ines
DISC-E2.caption: Three separate incidents. The repeated part is what matters.

DISC-E3.speaker: Mara
DISC-E3.caption: Good. Now we have two assumptions to test, instead of two people to blame.

DISC-E4.speaker: Ines
DISC-E4.caption: We tested this. We just never put the results in the same room.

DISC-E5.speaker: Mara
DISC-E5.caption: Read it twice. They're not picking a side. They want both.

MISMATCH-DEV-1.speaker: Dev
MISMATCH-DEV-1.caption: I see why you picked that. How does it support this particular setting?

MISMATCH-DEV-2.speaker: Dev
MISMATCH-DEV-2.caption: That tells us something useful, but it doesn't answer the question we're deciding here.

MISMATCH-DEV-3.speaker: Dev
MISMATCH-DEV-3.caption: Let's keep that for the other argument. What do we have for this one?

MISMATCH-DEV-4.speaker: Dev
MISMATCH-DEV-4.caption: I'm not seeing the connection yet. Which part of that evidence supports the choice?

MISMATCH-DEV-5.speaker: Dev
MISMATCH-DEV-5.caption: The evidence matters. We just need to match it to the right decision.

MISMATCH-INES-1.speaker: Ines
MISMATCH-INES-1.caption: That's real data. It just isn't evidence for this decision.

MISMATCH-INES-2.speaker: Ines
MISMATCH-INES-2.caption: Accurate, relevant to something, and not to this.

MISMATCH-INES-3.speaker: Ines
MISMATCH-INES-3.caption: Please connect it to the claim. I'll wait.

MISMATCH-INES-4.speaker: Ines
MISMATCH-INES-4.caption: I agree with every word of it, and it still doesn't help.

MISMATCH-INES-5.speaker: Ines
MISMATCH-INES-5.caption: You've brought a map of the wrong city.

MISMATCH-INES-6.speaker: Ines
MISMATCH-INES-6.caption: That supports a different argument. Save it.

MISMATCH-INES-7.speaker: Ines
MISMATCH-INES-7.caption: If I accept this, I have to accept anything. Try another.

MATCH-DEV-1.speaker: Dev
MATCH-DEV-1.caption: That makes sense. The result gives me a reason to reconsider.

MATCH-DEV-2.speaker: Dev
MATCH-DEV-2.caption: All right. That's something we can build a decision around.

MATCH-INES-2.speaker: Ines
MATCH-INES-2.caption: That's the first thing today I can build on.

MATCH-MARA-1.speaker: Mara
MATCH-MARA-1.caption: Careful. Persuading someone is not the same as being right. Make sure you have both.

EVENT-1.speaker: Mara
EVENT-1.caption: Warm-up batch. Nothing scary yet. Watch how smooth it is.

EVENT-2.speaker: Ines
EVENT-2.caption: A technician has stepped into the robot's path, forty centimetres away. The arm is still moving. Do we trust its stopping margin, or step in?

EVENT-3.speaker: Mara
EVENT-3.caption: A jam. Your recovery setting decides what happens next.

EVENT-4.speaker: Dev
EVENT-4.caption: An unfamiliar object is on the belt. Your confirmation setting decides whether the robot asks for help or tries to identify it alone.

EVENT-5.speaker: Mara
EVENT-5.caption: This is the one Northgate sees. Fingers crossed.

LETTER-01.speaker: Northgate
LETTER-01.caption: For the demonstration, we need to see TERN-1 work independently. We also need a documented way for a person to override it. Both are required.

EVIDENCE-SPEED-1.speaker: Mara
EVIDENCE-SPEED-1.caption: What did you find that supports this speed? Your case file has the evidence you collected.

EVIDENCE-SPEED-2.speaker: Mara
EVIDENCE-SPEED-2.caption: Which observation makes you comfortable with that speed?

EVIDENCE-RECOVERY-1.speaker: Mara
EVIDENCE-RECOVERY-1.caption: Which incident or test supports this recovery approach?

EVIDENCE-RECOVERY-2.speaker: Mara
EVIDENCE-RECOVERY-2.caption: What did the evidence tell you about clearing a jam safely?

EVIDENCE-LEARNING-1.speaker: Mara
EVIDENCE-LEARNING-1.caption: What supports how often the robot should ask for confirmation?

EVIDENCE-LEARNING-2.speaker: Mara
EVIDENCE-LEARNING-2.caption: Which finding helps us balance accuracy against interruptions?

CO-01.speaker: Mara
CO-01.caption: Robotics won't ship without full autonomy, and Software won't sign off without hard overrides. We have twelve weeks of runway and neither team will move.

CO-02.speaker: Dev
CO-02.caption: TERN-1 handles ninety-four percent of picks on its own. I want Northgate to see what that autonomy can do.

CO-03.speaker: Ines
CO-03.caption: Three near-misses in six weeks. This is not a feature request. — I.

CO-05.speaker: Mara
CO-05.caption: We want to see it run itself. Our auditor needs to see it stop.

CO-04.speaker: CONTROL
CO-04.caption: Twelve weeks. Two teams. One prototype. Walk the floor, then decide who moves.

CO-06.speaker: CONTROL
CO-06.caption: Inspect three things. You can't open everything.

FW-01a.speaker: Dev
FW-01a.caption: Most of the picks worked without help. The part we need to examine is where a person came too close.

FW-01b.speaker: Ines
FW-01b.caption: That's the crossing I flagged: forty centimetres from the moving arm.

FW-02a.speaker: Ines
FW-02a.caption: Three in six weeks. The e-stop wasn't even wired to the interlock.

FW-02b.speaker: Dev
FW-02b.caption: Those were bench tests, so let's be careful about treating them as the full demonstration.

FW-03a.speaker: Dev
FW-03a.caption: I'm concerned a speed cap will slow the demonstration too much. We need to understand that trade-off.

FW-03b.speaker: Ines
FW-03b.caption: Confirmation prompts cost nothing. Always have.

FW-03c.speaker: CONTROL
FW-03c.caption: Two assumptions. Nobody has tested either.

FW-04.speaker: Mara
FW-04.caption: BENCH-0914. Nobody's opened it. I was waiting for a reason.

FW-05a.speaker: CONTROL
FW-05a.caption: Both lines are in the same letter.

FW-05b.speaker: Mara
FW-05b.caption: Autonomy and overrides. They want both.

FW-06.speaker: CONTROL
FW-06.caption: Three looks. That's what the morning allows.

FW-07.speaker: CONTROL
FW-07.caption: You still have looks left. Go to the table anyway?

FW-08.speaker: Dev
FW-08.caption: The incident log matters. I'd also like us to look at how the robot performed before we choose a direction.

FW-09.speaker: Ines
FW-09.caption: You only looked at Dev's side.

T-INTRO.speaker: CONTROL
T-INTRO.caption: Three conflicts. Five alignment points. Move the tokens.

T-R-DEV.speaker: Dev
T-R-DEV.caption: That keeps the autonomous behavior I wanted to demonstrate. We need to explain how the safeguards fit around it.

T-R-INES.speaker: Ines
T-R-INES.caption: Noted. If it hits someone, this decision is on record.

T-S-INES.speaker: Ines
T-S-INES.caption: Thank you. The setting gets the guard rails.

T-S-DEV.speaker: Dev
T-S-DEV.caption: I understand the safety argument. I'm concerned about how much autonomy we'll be able to show with that choice.

T-B-DEV.speaker: Dev
T-B-DEV.caption: I'm open to a compromise. Let's make sure it still gives Northgate something useful to evaluate.

T-B-INES.speaker: Ines
T-B-INES.caption: Fine. Show me the version that stays safe.

T-D-DEV.speaker: Dev
T-D-DEV.caption: Leaving this open makes the build harder to plan. When are we going to settle it?

T-EV-CON.speaker: Mara
T-EV-CON.caption: That says the opposite of your call.

T-EV-NEU.speaker: Mara
T-EV-NEU.caption: That doesn't speak to this one.

T-EV-NONE.speaker: Mara
T-EV-NONE.caption: What did the evidence tell you? You can check your case file before you commit.

T-AP.speaker: CONTROL
T-AP.caption: A bridge costs two points and a week.

C1-ALIGNED.speaker: Mara
C1-ALIGNED.caption: The compromises give both leads a place in the plan. They've cost us time, but we now have a direction they can work on together.

C1-ROBOTICS.speaker: Mara
C1-ROBOTICS.caption: You backed Dev on most of the arguments. His plan moves forward, but Ines still has safety concerns. We need to address those before the demonstration.

C1-SOFTWARE.speaker: Mara
C1-SOFTWARE.caption: You backed Ines on most of the arguments. The safeguards stay, but Dev feels sidelined. We need him involved in the next decision.

C1-STALLED.speaker: Mara
C1-STALLED.caption: Several arguments are still unresolved. The team cannot build around an incomplete plan, and the delay will cost us more runway.

C1-MIXED.speaker: Mara
C1-MIXED.caption: You've split the decisions between the two leads. They still need a shared reason to trust the plan. Next, give them the same evidence to work from.

O2-A1.speaker: Mara
O2-A1.caption: You bought us alignment. It cost weeks. Use them.

O2-R1.speaker: Nadia
O2-R1.caption: Mind if I sit in? Northgate asked me to.

O2-R2.speaker: Ines
O2-R2.caption: She's here for the override evidence.

O2-S1.speaker: Dev
O2-S1.caption: I've been considering another role. I'd like to stay involved here, but I need to see a plan that uses the work we've done.

O2-T1.speaker: Mara
O2-T1.caption: We're out of time to be polite.

O2-M1.speaker: Mara
O2-M1.caption: Half a plan, two tired leads. Pick what they see.

O2-CTRL.speaker: CONTROL
O2-CTRL.caption: Four sealed folders. Whatever you project, both teams see.

O2-14.speaker: Dev
O2-14.caption: Thanks for calling me back. Walk me through the evidence so I can understand the build you're proposing.

O2-15.speaker: Dev
O2-15.caption: All right, show me the test results. I want to understand what they change.

O2-16.speaker: Dev
O2-16.caption: I don't think we're making room for the robotics concerns. I'm going to step out for now.

S-D1-DEV.speaker: Dev
S-D1-DEV.caption: So the cap costs six percent of throughput, not thirty. That changes the trade-off.

S-D1-INES.speaker: Ines
S-D1-INES.caption: I told you the cap was cheap.

S-D2-DEV.speaker: Dev
S-D2-DEV.caption: Unattended accuracy is eighty-one percent. I expected better than that. We need a way to check unfamiliar objects.

S-D2-INES.speaker: Ines
S-D2-INES.caption: Thirty-one percent of picks interrupted? I was wrong about prompts.

S-D2-MARA.speaker: Mara
S-D2-MARA.caption: First time they've agreed on anything.

S-D3-INES.speaker: Ines
S-D3-INES.caption: With the curtain, the robot stops in twenty-two centimetres at one metre per second. That's inside our forty-centimetre limit. The faster setting isn't.

S-D3-DEV.speaker: Dev
S-D3-DEV.caption: Then one metre per second is a practical option. We keep most of the throughput and stay inside that measured margin.

S-D4-DEV.speaker: Dev
S-D4-DEV.caption: So the interlock isn't what's causing the jams. We should focus on the calibration and recovery behavior.

S-D4-INES.speaker: Ines
S-D4-INES.caption: And auto-recovery is fine, with the interlock.

S-NAD-NO.speaker: Nadia
S-NAD-NO.caption: No override evidence in this meeting. Noted.

S-VETO-R.speaker: Dev
S-VETO-R.caption: I'd like to keep automatic recovery in the build. If we change it, I need evidence that the alternative will work.

S-VETO-S.speaker: Ines
S-VETO-S.caption: The speed cap stays at half a metre per second until we've addressed the safety concern.

S-END.speaker: Mara
S-END.caption: Enough data. Build something they'll both sign.

F-INTRO.speaker: CONTROL
F-INTRO.caption: Three dials. A question mark means you never opened that folder.

F-ACC-DEV.speaker: Dev
F-ACC-DEV.caption: That gives us enough autonomy to show what the robot can do. My team can build this.

F-REJ-DEV-1.speaker: Dev
F-REJ-DEV-1.caption: At that speed, I'm not confident we can demonstrate the value of autonomous sorting. Can we reconsider the cap?

F-REJ-DEV-2.speaker: Dev
F-REJ-DEV-2.caption: Manual recovery means someone has to clear every jam. I'd like the prototype to handle more of that itself.

F-REJ-DEV-3.speaker: Dev
F-REJ-DEV-3.caption: If an operator confirms every object, we lose much of the benefit of learning. Can we make those checks more selective?

F-REJ-INES-1.speaker: Ines
F-REJ-INES-1.caption: Show me the margin at that speed.

F-REJ-INES-2.speaker: Ines
F-REJ-INES-2.caption: No self-recovery without the interlock data.

F-REJ-INES-3.speaker: Ines
F-REJ-INES-3.caption: That learning setting has no tuned threshold.

F-REJ-INES-4.speaker: Ines
F-REJ-INES-4.caption: Never confirming is not an option.

F-PUSH-DEV.speaker: Dev
F-PUSH-DEV.caption: I don't agree with that choice, but I understand you're moving ahead. I'll make sure my concerns are documented.

F-IMP.speaker: Mara
F-IMP.caption: I'm calling it. Lean build. Move.

F-RUNWAY.speaker: CONTROL
F-RUNWAY.caption: Reserve: two weeks for the run.

C2-AGREED.speaker: Mara
C2-AGREED.caption: One build. Two signatures. Don't waste it.

C2-IMPOSED.speaker: Mara
C2-IMPOSED.caption: It's the safe build. It won't impress anyone.

RN-E1-H.speaker: CONTROL
RN-E1-H.caption: Event one. Warm-up batch. Hands off.

RN-E1-FAST.speaker: Dev
RN-E1-FAST.caption: That's the cycle time I was hoping for. The robot is keeping the tray moving without help.

RN-E1-SLOW.speaker: Dev
RN-E1-SLOW.caption: It's slower than I wanted, but the movement is controlled and the tray is still progressing.

RN-E2-H1.speaker: CONTROL
RN-E2-H1.caption: A technician has crossed into the cell, forty centimetres from the moving arm.

RN-E2-ASK.speaker: CONTROL
RN-E2-ASK.caption: Let it run, or step in.

RN-INT-SLOW.speaker: Dev
RN-INT-SLOW.caption: We've slowed the arm to handle this step safely. The interruption will be visible to Northgate.

RN-INT-TAKE.speaker: Dev
RN-INT-TAKE.caption: An operator is handling this step now. We'll need to be clear with Northgate about that support.

RN-E3-MAN.speaker: Dev
RN-E3-MAN.caption: The arm is waiting while someone clears the jam. That's the manual recovery setting we chose.

RN-E3-ASS.speaker: Dev
RN-E3-ASS.caption: One confirmation from the operator, and the recovery starts. The robot can take it from here.

RN-E3-AUTO.speaker: Dev
RN-E3-AUTO.caption: The robot cleared the jam without an operator stepping in. That's the recovery behavior I wanted to demonstrate.

RN-E4-H.speaker: CONTROL
RN-E4-H.caption: Event four. An object it has never seen.

RN-E4-ALW.speaker: Dev
RN-E4-ALW.caption: The robot is asking the operator to confirm this object. With this setting, it will ask on every pick.

RN-E4-UNC.speaker: Dev
RN-E4-UNC.caption: It asked for help on the unfamiliar object, then continued. It doesn't have to interrupt the operator on every pick.

EN-01.speaker: Mara
EN-01.caption: Everyone was careful. Nothing was built.

EN-02.speaker: Theo
EN-02.caption: I think we should postpone the demonstration. Let me know when the prototype is ready for us to evaluate.

EN-03.speaker: CONTROL
EN-03.caption: The runway ran down four more weeks.

EN-F1.speaker: Nadia
EN-F1.caption: The override failed with a technician forty centimetres away. I can't sign off on that demonstration.

EN-F2.speaker: Theo
EN-F2.caption: I can't recommend this version to my partners after what we just saw. We need to understand the failure before we go further.

EN-F3.speaker: Mara
EN-F3.caption: Then we find out what broke.

EN-G1.speaker: Nadia
EN-G1.caption: Documented overrides, demonstrated autonomy. I'll sign.

EN-G2.speaker: Theo
EN-G2.caption: The demonstration was convincing. What gives me confidence is that the team can explain the trade-offs and stand behind the same build.

EN-G4.speaker: Dev
EN-G4.caption: We both changed the plan once we saw the results. It helped to work from the same evidence.

EN-W1.speaker: Theo
EN-W1.caption: There's impressive work here. Before we go further, how much supervision would this need in one of our warehouses?

EN-W3.speaker: Dev
EN-W3.caption: That level of supervision isn't where I want the product to end up. We still have work to do.

EN-B1.speaker: Theo
EN-B1.caption: I can see that it works with the team helping. I need to know whether it can handle a normal shift without that level of support.

EN-S1.speaker: Theo
EN-S1.caption: This looks dependable. The next question for us is whether it creates enough value to justify putting it into a warehouse.

EN-END.speaker: CONTROL
EN-END.caption: The run is over. The room remembers.

T-EV-SUP-DEV.speaker: Dev
T-EV-SUP-DEV.caption: That finding helps me understand the decision. I can work with that evidence.

sfx: Procedural WebAudio; dialogue is pre-rendered MP3.
